answer.pull.above-tier.bare.text: Dinah found ready work to pull, but none of it meets your declared tier
answer.pull.above-tier.bare.context: The one-line sentence pull prints when the bare form was asked, a column holds ready work, and the tier the caller declared is admitted for none of it. It is a separate key from answer.pull.empty.bare on purpose, because a caller reading the message alone has to be able to tell work standing above it from no work at all.

answer.pull.above-tier.named.text: Dinah found ready work in {upstream} for {destination}, but none of it meets your declared tier
answer.pull.above-tier.named.context: The one-line sentence pull prints when the named form was asked, a source holds ready work, and the tier the caller declared is admitted for none of it. {upstream} names the source column by its title, {destination} names the column the caller asked pull to land the card in. It is a separate key from answer.pull.empty.named on purpose, because a caller reading the message alone has to be able to tell work standing above it from no work at all.

answer.pull.empty.bare.text: Dinah found no column you can pull into right now
answer.pull.empty.bare.context: The one-line sentence the empty answer of pull prints when the bare form was asked and nothing qualifies. It is the answer the refusal table explicitly carves out as an answer rather than a refusal, and the cardless OK response carries the catalog key the head renders.

answer.pull.empty.named.text: Dinah found nothing ready in {upstream} to move into {destination}
answer.pull.empty.named.context: The one-line sentence the empty answer of pull prints when the named form was asked and the upstream column holds no ready card this pull may take, which since routes includes an upstream whose ready cards are all bound somewhere else. {upstream} names the upstream column by its title, {destination} names the column the caller asked pull to land the card in.

attachments.empty.context: Printed when `dinah list attachments` is asked about an entity that carries none. No table follows, and the call succeeds: an entity with nothing attached is an answer rather than a mistake.

attachments.header.context: The sentence above the table `dinah list attachments` prints, naming the entity the attachments hang from. {count} is how many that entity carries.

card.blocked.context: Printed under the card line when the card is blocked.

card.field.context: Printed under the card line for one field this workbench declares that the card carries a value for, one line per field, in declaration order. {field} is the declared key and {value} is what the card stores under it, both read off the store rather than written here, so both are machine vocabulary and neither is translated.

card.holder.context: Printed under the card line when somebody holds the card.

card.inapplicable.context: Printed by show under the card line for one level axis or declared key that does not apply to the card and that the card stores nothing for, naming the gating field and what the card stores under it. {field}, {gate} and {value} are read off the workbench and the card, so all three are machine vocabulary and none is translated.

card.inapplicable.stored.text: {field}: {stored}, kept although it does not apply, because {gate} is {value}
card.inapplicable.stored.context: Printed on every surface that draws card lines, in place of the ordinary line for one level axis or declared key, when the card stores a value there that its applies_when condition no longer admits. {field} is the axis or key, {stored} is the kept value, {gate} is the gating field and {value} is what the card stores under it; all four are read off the workbench and the card and none is translated.

card.inapplicable.stored-unset.text: {field}: {stored}, kept although it does not apply, because {gate} carries no value
card.inapplicable.stored-unset.context: The sibling of card.inapplicable.stored printed when the card stores no value under the gating field at all. {field}, {stored} and {gate} are read off the workbench and the card and never translated.

card.inapplicable.unset.text: {field}: does not apply, because {gate} carries no value
card.inapplicable.unset.context: The sibling of card.inapplicable printed when the card stores no value under the gating field at all. {field} and {gate} are read off the workbench and never translated.

card.line.context: The one line printed about a card after an act.

card.line.workstreams.context: The one line printed about a card that belongs to at least one workstream, after an act. It is card.line with the memberships on the end, and the caller chooses between the two by whether the card lists any. {workstreams} holds the workstreams already joined by card.line.workstreams.separator.

card.line.workstreams.separator.context: What separates two workstreams inside the {workstreams} field of card.line.workstreams. A punctuation mark and whatever spacing the language wants around it.

card.priority.context: Printed under the card line when the card carries a priority.

card.retirement-grant.context: Printed under the card line when the card carries a standing criterion-retirement authorization. {column} is the reference of the column the grant is bound to and {title} is that column's title; the reference is machine vocabulary and is never translated. A card carrying no grant draws no such line.

card.severity.context: Printed under the card line when the card carries a severity.

changes.cursor.context: The line printed under the events of `dinah changes`, carrying the token to hand back at the next call. {cursor} is that token, which a caller treats as opaque.

check.active-without-claim.text: card {detail} reads active and carries no holder
check.active-without-claim.context: A check finding: the converse of the claim implication.

check.add.1.context: One row of the precondition list of a command outside the five the profile specifies.

check.add.2.context: One row of the precondition list of a command outside the five the profile specifies.

check.applies-when-below-format.text: this workbench uses applies_when but declares format {detail}; run `dinah check --migrate-applies-when --yes` so that an older Dinah refuses it instead of misreading it
check.applies-when-below-format.context: A check finding: a workbench whose definition carries an applies_when member or a level axis in mapping form while declaring a storage format below the one that introduced them. {detail} carries the declared format number. An older Dinah reads such a levels block wrongly rather than incompletely, which is what the format number exists to prevent, and the command line inside the sentence is the repair and stays as it is.

check.applies-when-malformed.text: the applies_when condition on {detail} cannot be used, so the declaration it sits on applies to every card
check.applies-when-malformed.context: A check finding: an applies_when member the reader refused. {detail} carries the level axis or the declared key it sits on and then, in parentheses, the reason token: unreadable, tier, reaches-beyond-cards, gate-undeclared, gate-off-cards or gate-conditioned. The condition is ignored, so the axis or the key applies to every card, and the repair is an edit to the workbench anchor. The sentence says declaration rather than field because the slot may be a level axis.

check.applies-when-value-unmatchable.text: the applies_when condition on {detail} names a value its gating field can never hold
check.applies-when-value-unmatchable.context: A check finding: one value in a usable applies_when condition's is list that the gating field's declared type refuses, so no card can ever store it and none is ever admitted by it. {detail} carries the level axis or the declared key and then the value in parentheses. The rest of the condition stands, and the repair is an edit to the workbench anchor.

check.archive.4.context: One row of the precondition list of a command outside the five the profile specifies.

check.at-loop-limit.text: column {detail} declares a loop_limit this card has already reached, so its next regressive move is refused
check.at-loop-limit.context: A check finding: the card standing at this column has left it backwards as often as the column's loop_limit allows. {detail} carries the declaring column.

check.attach.1.context: One row of the precondition list of a command outside the five the profile specifies.

check.attach.2.context: One row of the precondition list of a command outside the five the profile specifies.

check.attach.3.context: One row of the precondition list of a command outside the five the profile specifies.

check.attach.5.context: One row of the precondition list of a command outside the five the profile specifies.

check.attachment-filename-drift.text: attachment {detail} payload file name disagrees with its anchor
check.attachment-filename-drift.context: A check finding: an attachment's payload file and its anchor's filename field disagree, which is the residue of a crash between a rename's two writes or of a hand edit nobody noticed.

check.attachments-without-a-mount.text: {detail} carries an attachments directory, and Dinah keeps no attachments on {detail}, so nothing reaches the files inside it
check.attachments-without-a-mount.context: A check finding: an attachments directory sitting below an entity of a kind that holds no attachments. {detail} names that kind, which is machine vocabulary and is never translated. The path beside the sentence is the directory itself, because the reader has to open it to decide what to do with the files. Dinah does not remove it, because the files belong to whoever attached them.

check.bare-workbench.text: the workbench.md at {detail} sits outside any .dinah container, so no search finds it; dinah check --migrate-container creates a .dinah container inside {detail} and moves the workbench's own files into it, leaving everything else in {detail} where it stands
check.bare-workbench.context: A check finding: a directory carrying a workbench.md Dinah recognises as its own, sitting outside any container, which the containment rule means is no longer a workbench. {detail} carries that directory.

check.block-without-reason.text: card {detail} is blocked and carries no reason
check.block-without-reason.context: A check finding: every blocked card carries a reason.

check.block.1.context: One row of the ordered precondition list of block, quoted from section 6 of the core profile.

check.block.2.context: One row of the ordered precondition list of block, quoted from section 6 of the core profile.

check.block.3.context: One row of the ordered precondition list of block, quoted from section 6 of the core profile.

check.block.4.text: the card is unheld or held by whoever asks
check.block.4.context: One row of the ordered precondition list of block, quoted from section 6 of the core profile.

check.branch-conflict.anchor-differs.text: {card} already stores a different value for that field
check.branch-conflict.anchor-differs.context: One row of the branch migration's conflict report: a card whose stored value for the declared field differs from the value its body carries, so the run cannot tell which of the two the operator meant. {card} carries the card's reference.

check.branch-conflict.two-headings.text: {card} carries that heading more than once
check.branch-conflict.two-headings.context: One row of the branch migration's conflict report: a card whose body carries the retired heading more than once, so the run cannot tell which of them is the value. {card} carries the card's reference.

check.branch-conflict.unreadable.text: {card} will not open, so the run could not read it
check.branch-conflict.unreadable.context: One row of the branch migration's conflict report: a card whose anchor will not open, so the run cannot classify it and will not write a workbench it has not read whole. {card} carries the card's identifier.

check.branch-emptied.text: {card} lost a heading with nothing under it.
check.branch-emptied.context: One line of the branch migration's own report, naming a card that carried the retired heading with nothing beneath it. Such a card loses the heading and gains no value, so it is named rather than counted alone. {card} carries the card's reference.

check.branch-heading-in-body.text: {detail} still carries the retired heading in its body, which this store's format says was lifted into a declared field
check.branch-heading-in-body.context: A check finding: a card whose body still carries the retired heading, on a workbench whose declared format says that heading was lifted into a declared field. {detail} carries the card's reference. A workbench declaring a lower format is not reported, because it has not been carried across the retirement and the heading is still its convention.

check.branch-lift.context: One line of the branch migration's own report, naming a card and the value the migration lifted out of its body into the declared field. {card} carries the card's reference and {branch} the value now stored under that field, both read off the store, so both are machine vocabulary and neither is translated.

check.branch-would-empty.text: {card} would lose a heading with nothing under it.
check.branch-would-empty.context: One line of the branch migration's preview, naming a card that carries the retired heading with nothing beneath it. A confirmed run would take the heading away and write no value. {card} carries the card's reference.

check.branch-would-lift.context: One line of the branch migration's preview, naming a card and the value a confirmed run would lift out of its body into the declared field. It is spelled apart from check.branch-lift because a preview writes nothing, and the same sentence under both would tell an operator a write had happened. {card} carries the card's reference and {branch} the value the body holds, both read off the store, so both are machine vocabulary and neither is translated.

check.branches-conflicted.one.text: Wrote nothing, because {count} card cannot be carried across:
check.branches-conflicted.one.context: The heading over the cards the classification refused, for exactly one card. A single one of them stops the run before any write, so the rows beneath name what has to be repaired before a second run completes.

check.branches-conflicted.other.text: Wrote nothing, because {count} cards cannot be carried across:
check.branches-conflicted.other.context: The heading over the cards the classification refused, for any other number. A single one of them stops the run before any write, so the rows beneath name what has to be repaired before a second run completes.

check.branches-declared.context: The line the branch migration prints when it added the declaration for the key it lifted into. A workbench that already declared the key keeps its own declaration and this line is not printed. {field} carries the key, read off the store, so it is machine vocabulary and is never translated.

check.branches-emptied.one.text: Removed an empty heading from {count} card:
check.branches-emptied.one.context: The heading over the cards that carried the retired heading with nothing beneath it, for exactly one card. Each loses the heading and gains no value, so they are named rather than counted alone.

check.branches-emptied.other.text: Removed an empty heading from {count} cards:
check.branches-emptied.other.context: The heading over the cards that carried the retired heading with nothing beneath it, for any other number. Each loses the heading and gains no value, so they are named rather than counted alone.

check.branches-lifted.one.text: {count} card carries a value to lift.
check.branches-lifted.one.context: The line the branch migration prints for what its classification found to lift, for exactly one card. It reports the classification rather than the write, so it reads the same whether the run went on to write or stopped at a conflict.

check.branches-lifted.other.text: {count} cards carry a value to lift.
check.branches-lifted.other.context: The line the branch migration prints for what its classification found to lift, for any other number. A count of zero is a run that found no heading to lift, which is that run's own answer.

check.branches-preview.text: Nothing was written, because this run carried no confirmation.
check.branches-preview.context: The first line the branch migration prints when it ran without the confirmation flag, so that a reader cannot take the counts below it for work that happened.

check.branches-stamped.context: The line the branch migration prints when it wrote the format number onto the workbench anchor, which is what says the retirement has happened here. {format} carries the number.

check.branches-untouched.one.context: The line the branch migration prints for the cards its classification found nothing to do to, for exactly one card. It is printed beside the count above so that a run which classified nothing cannot read as a run which found nothing to do.

check.branches-untouched.other.context: The line the branch migration prints for the cards its classification found nothing to do to, for any other number. It is printed beside the count above so that a run which classified nothing cannot read as a run which found nothing to do.

check.branches-would-empty.one.text: An empty heading would be removed from {count} card:
check.branches-would-empty.one.context: The heading over the cards carrying the retired heading with nothing beneath it, in the branch migration's preview, for exactly one card.

check.branches-would-empty.other.text: An empty heading would be removed from {count} cards:
check.branches-would-empty.other.context: The heading over the cards carrying the retired heading with nothing beneath it, in the branch migration's preview, for any other number.

check.card-number-duplicate.text: {detail} claims a number that another line claims too, so a reference by number answers with more than one card
check.card-number-duplicate.context: A check finding: two or more lines of the card-number registry claim one number, which leaves the durable half of a card reference ambiguous. {detail} carries the line as stored, which is what a reader searches the file for. `dinah check --renumber --yes` repairs it, moving every later claimant.

check.card-number-in-frontmatter.text: {detail} still carries a number key in its anchor, on a workbench whose registry is the number's home
check.card-number-in-frontmatter.context: A check finding: a card of a workbench declaring the registry's format that still carries a number key in its anchor, which the migration strips and nothing else writes. {detail} carries the card's identifier. `dinah check --migrate-numbers --yes` strips it.

check.card-number-malformed.text: {detail} is not a line the registry's grammar reads, so it claims no number and no card
check.card-number-malformed.context: A check finding: a line of card-numbers.txt that does not parse under the registry's grammar. {detail} carries the line verbatim, which is what a reader searches the file for. No marker repairs it; the operator rewrites the line by hand.

check.card-number-missing.text: {detail} has no line in the card-number registry, so no number names it
check.card-number-missing.context: A check finding: a card in either half of the collection that no line of the card-number registry claims. {detail} carries the card's identifier. A workbench still declaring the older format draws this for every card it holds, which is the flood that ends when `dinah check --migrate-numbers --yes` builds the registry.

check.card-number-renumbered.text: {detail} was renumbered, so a reference somebody wrote down for its old number stops resolving
check.card-number-renumbered.context: A check finding a number repair raises: the card left the run holding a number it did not arrive holding. The renumbered event on the card's journal says the same thing where history keeps it. {detail} carries the card's identifier.

check.card-number-repeated.text: {detail} is one of two or more lines naming one card, so the card answers to more than one number
check.card-number-repeated.context: A check finding: two or more lines of the card-number registry name one identifier, so one card holds two numbers. {detail} carries the line as stored, which is what a reader searches the file for. No marker repairs it, because choosing what a card is called is the operator's.

check.card-number-stranded.text: {detail} names neither a card nor a tombstone, so the number it claims is held by nothing
check.card-number-stranded.context: A check finding: a line of the card-number registry whose identifier is neither a tombstone nor a card in either half of the collection. {detail} carries the line as stored, which is what a reader searches the file for. No marker removes it, because removing the line would release the number for reuse, which is the operator's call.

check.card-numbers-written.one.text: Wrote {count} line of the card-number registry.
check.card-numbers-written.one.context: The line the number migration prints for what it wrote, for exactly one line.

check.card-numbers-written.other.text: Wrote {count} lines of the card-number registry.
check.card-numbers-written.other.context: The line the number migration prints for what it wrote, for any other number. The count is zero on a run over a workbench whose registry already covered every card, which is that run's own answer.

check.card-vocabulary-mixed.text: card {detail} carries a key from each of the two vocabularies this format has had, so its standing cannot be read
check.card-vocabulary-mixed.context: A check finding: a card whose header holds half of each vocabulary. The checker reports what the reader refuses under dinah.vocabulary-mixed, so a card whose anchor file is plainly there is not reported as having none.

check.card-vocabulary-retired.text: card {detail} is written in the vocabulary this format retired, and this workbench declares the current one, so its standing cannot be read
check.card-vocabulary-retired.context: A check finding: a card the rename never carried across, inside a workbench whose own anchor says it was. The checker reports what the reader refuses under dinah.vocabulary-retired, so a card whose anchor file is plainly there is not reported as having none.

check.cards-renumbered.one.context: The line a number repair prints for what it moved, for exactly one card. The moved cards are counted and not listed, because each draws a check.card-number-renumbered finding naming it immediately below.

check.cards-renumbered.other.context: The line a number repair prints for what it moved, for any other number. The moved cards are counted and not listed, because each draws a check.card-number-renumbered finding naming it immediately below.

The acts that would create the condition afresh are refused, so a card reported here was written before this build.

check.claim-without-active.context: A check finding: the claim fields and state active imply each other.

check.claim.10.text: this call declared a provider and a model
check.claim.10.context: One row of the ordered precondition list of claim. It is the third of the three answers the tier gate can refuse with, and it reports dinah.undeclared-model. Its reader is a harness nobody configured rather than one running the wrong model.

check.claim.2.context: One row of the ordered precondition list of claim, quoted from section 6 of the core profile.

check.claim.3.text: the owner named as holder is the owner asking
check.claim.3.context: One row of the ordered precondition list of claim, quoted from section 6 of the core profile.

check.claim.6.context: One row of the ordered precondition list of claim, quoted from section 6 of the core profile.

check.claim.7.text: every unresolved item the card carries names a declared column
check.claim.7.context: One row of the ordered precondition list of claim, quoted from section 6 of the core profile.

check.claim.8.text: your model resolves at or above what the card asks
check.claim.8.context: One row of the ordered precondition list of claim. This row is Dinah's own addition; the core profile's own section 6.3 list ends at check.claim.7. What the card asks for is its own baseline or its override for this column, never the column's own default. The tier a model resolves to is read off the workbench's own tiers table rather than declared by the caller, and a workbench that declares no table refuses nobody here. The row is kept short because the table it prints in is bounded by the reader's window.

check.claim.9.text: this workbench's table lists the model you declared
check.claim.9.context: One row of the ordered precondition list of claim. It is the second of the three answers the tier gate can refuse with, and it reports dinah.unlisted-model. The row is kept short because the table it prints in is bounded by the reader's window.

check.column-body-limit-malformed.text: workbench.md declares column_body_limit as {detail}, which is not a whole number of bytes above zero, so no column body is measured against it
check.column-body-limit-malformed.context: A check finding at defect severity: the workbench's column_body_limit is not a positive whole number, so no body is measured. {detail} carries the value as stored.

check.column-body-over-limit.text: column {detail}: the body's size in bytes is larger than the column_body_limit this workbench declares, so move what a station reads only when a situation arises into an attachment on the column
check.column-body-over-limit.context: A check finding at cleanup severity. {detail} carries the column's reference, then the body's size and the declared limit in bytes written as size/limit, such as `review 5120/4096`. The repair is the author's: shorten the body, or raise or remove the workbench's column_body_limit.

check.container-already.other.context: The heading over the workbenches the container migration left alone because they already sit where the rule puts one, for any other number.

check.container-confirm.text: Nothing was written. This repair moves directories, so read the list above before you authorize it, then run the same command again with --yes.

check.container-damaged.one.text: {count} workbench sits where the rule puts one and no longer reads as a Dinah anchor; it was not touched.
check.container-damaged.one.context: The heading over the damaged workbenches a container sweep found, for exactly one. Each row names the directory. The sweep reports them and repairs none of them, because the repair is content rather than position.

check.container-damaged.other.context: The heading over the damaged workbenches a container sweep found, for any other number.

check.container-duplicate.one.text: {count} workbench identifier is claimed by more than one directory, and none of them was touched.
check.container-duplicate.one.context: The heading over the duplicated workbench identifiers a sweep found, for exactly one. Each row names the identifier and every path claiming it.

check.container-duplicate.other.text: {count} workbench identifiers are claimed by more than one directory, and none of them was touched.
check.container-duplicate.other.context: The heading over the duplicated workbench identifiers a sweep found, for any other number.

check.container-failed.one.text: {count} workbench could not be carried into a container.
check.container-failed.one.context: The heading over the workbenches the container migration could not move, for exactly one. Each row names the directory and the reason.

check.container-failed.other.text: {count} workbenches could not be carried into a container.

check.designation-missing.context: A check finding: an item settled without an answer of record, which the designation conversion leaves behind wherever the history could not say which comment the answer meant. {detail} is the state the item keeps, machine vocabulary that is never translated.

check.designations-archived.one.text: {count} converted item carries an archived comment.
check.designations-archived.one.context: The line the designation conversion prints for the converted items whose comments hold at least one archived member, for exactly one item. That is the population whose positions may already have drifted before anybody ran the conversion.

check.designations-archived.other.text: {count} converted items carry an archived comment.
check.designations-archived.other.context: The line the designation conversion prints for the converted items whose comments hold at least one archived member, for any other number.

check.designations-claim.context: One card a forced designation conversion passed the claim of, drawn under the count. {card} is the card's reference and {owner} is who held it, and both are machine vocabulary that is never translated.

check.designations-claims-passed.one.context: The line a forced designation conversion prints for the claims it passed, for exactly one card. The same cards are named in the workbench's own history, so the judgement stays readable afterwards.

check.designations-claims-passed.other.context: The line a forced designation conversion prints for the claims it passed, for any other number, zero included, so that the flag is never a silent no-op.

check.designations-entry.text: {item}, settled by {settling}, now names {comment}, written by {author}.
check.designations-entry.context: One item a designation conversion converted, drawn under its group's count. {item} is the item's reference, {settling} is the journal event that last settled it, {comment} is the identifier the run wrote and {author} is who wrote that comment; all four are machine vocabulary that is never translated.

check.designations-journal-inferred.text: The items above were recovered from the history rather than from what was stored, because a removal since they were settled may have moved the positions. The history records whole seconds, so where a settling followed another comment of the same item inside one second, the comment named above may not be the one it meant. Read those before you rely on them.
check.designations-journal-inferred.context: The caution the designation conversion prints under its journal group, drawn only where that group holds an entry. It is the disclosure of the one case the conversion cannot decide: an item reaches that group only where a removal since the settling may have moved the stored positions and where a comment of the same item was written in the settling's own second, and the stamp carries seconds, so the comment it matched need not be the one the settling meant. It stands over the group rather than over the archived listing beside it, because a deleted comment leaves nothing in the archive to find and a deletion is the removal this case most often turns on.

check.designations-journal.one.context: The line the designation conversion prints for the items it recovered from the card's own history, for exactly one item. The history named the comment outright, so nothing was inferred.

check.designations-journal.other.context: The line the designation conversion prints for the items it recovered from the card's own history, for any other number.

check.designations-keeps-state.text: Each item above keeps the state it stands at and has lost its answer of record.
check.designations-keeps-state.context: The sentence the designation conversion prints once under the unanswered items, so that nobody reads the group as work the run undid.

check.designations-reaches.context: The clause an unanswered line of the designation conversion's report names whose comment the stored reference reaches today. {author} is that comment's author, which is a name rather than prose and is never translated, so no word of the clause may agree with it.

check.designations-reaches-nothing.context: The clause an unanswered line of the designation conversion's report carries in place of the one above where the stored reference reaches no comment of that item at all, which is the case a removal since the settling leaves behind. It names the absence rather than leaving the sentence to trail off.

check.designations-rehearsed.text: Nothing was written. Run it again without --rehearse to convert and stamp the workbench.
check.designations-rehearsed.context: The closing line of a rehearsal of the designation conversion, which decides everything and writes nothing. --rehearse is a flag name and is not translated.

check.designations-stamped.text: Stamped format {detail} on the workbench anchor.
check.designations-stamped.context: The closing line of a converting run of the designation conversion. {detail} is the format number it wrote, machine vocabulary that is never translated.

check.designations-unanswered-entry.text: {item}, settled by {settling}, keeps {state}; it stored {stored}, which reaches {reaches} today.
check.designations-unanswered-entry.context: One item a designation conversion left unanswered, drawn under the count. {item} is the item's reference, {settling} is the journal event that last settled it, {state} is the state it keeps, {stored} is the reference it carried before the run and {reaches} is the clause naming whose comment that reference reaches today; all are machine vocabulary or composed from it and are never translated. The author is named so the operator can see what a guessing conversion would have written down. An item whose journal records no settling at all takes the unsettled form beside this one rather than leaving that slot blank.

check.designations-unanswered-entry-unse.text: {item} keeps {state} and its history records no settling; it stored {stored}, which reaches {reaches} today.
check.designations-unanswered-entry-unse.context: One item a designation conversion left unanswered whose card journal records no settling for it at all, drawn under the count beside the ordinary form. {item} is the item's reference, {state} is the state it keeps and {reaches} is the clause naming whose comment the stored reference reaches today; all are machine vocabulary or composed from it and are never translated. It exists because the ordinary form names the settling verb and an item with none would leave that slot blank, which reads as a fault in the line the operator is told to act on.

check.designations-unanswered-total.one.text: {count} item is waiting for somebody to answer it again.
check.designations-unanswered-total.one.context: The last line of a designation conversion that left anything unanswered, for exactly one item, because that is the number the operator acts on.

check.designations-unanswered-total.othe.text: {count} items are waiting for somebody to answer them again.
check.designations-unanswered-total.othe.context: The last line of a designation conversion that left anything unanswered, for any other number.

check.designations-unanswered.one.context: The line the designation conversion prints for the items whose answer the history could not recover, for exactly one item. The conversion does not guess, so such an item is left unanswered.

check.designations-unanswered.other.context: The line the designation conversion prints for the items whose answer the history could not recover, for any other number.

check.designations-undisturbed.one.context: The line the designation conversion prints for the items nothing had disturbed since they were settled, for exactly one item. It is kept apart from the history group because the confidence is of a different kind.

check.designations-undisturbed.other.context: The line the designation conversion prints for the items nothing had disturbed since they were settled, for any other number.

check.evidence-scheme-undeclared.context: A check finding at cleanup severity, reported only where the workbench declares an evidence block. Two shapes share the key and {detail} tells them apart: a column's standing entry carries the column's reference, the entry key and the scheme, and a live item carrying an evidence key carries the card's reference, the item's identifier and the scheme. The repair is the author's: declare the scheme in the evidence block, or name one it declares.

check.field-declaration-malformed.text: the fields block declares {detail} with no usable type or meaning, so nothing is declared under that key
check.field-declaration-malformed.context: A check finding: one entry of this workbench's fields block that the declaration reader refused, which is an entry whose key the grammar refuses, whose type is absent or outside the five, or whose meaning is absent or blank. {detail} carries the key as written. The entry declares nothing and the workbench still opens, so the repair is an edit to the block.

check.view-malformed.text: a view in dinah.views cannot be read, so it cannot be drawn: {detail}
check.view-malformed.context: A check finding: one view of this workbench's dinah.views block that cannot be drawn. {detail} carries the view's name and a machine token naming its defect, or `dinah.views not-a-mapping` where the block itself is not a mapping. dinah.views is the key the views are declared under and is never translated.

check.view-member-unknown.text: a view in dinah.views carries a member this build does not read, and it is ignored: {detail}
check.view-member-unknown.context: A check finding at cleanup severity: a member of one of this workbench's views that this build does not read, such as a misspelt title. {detail} carries the view's name and the member's path, `sections/<n>/<member>` for a member of a section. The member is kept in the file and ignored, because a later build may read it.

check.view-query-refused.text: a view in dinah.views asks a question this workbench refuses: {detail}
check.view-query-refused.context: A check finding at cleanup severity: a section of one of this workbench's views whose query this workbench refuses, such as one naming a column the workbench no longer has. {detail} carries the view's name, the section's one-based position and the refusal's machine name.

check.urgency-malformed.text: the dinah.urgency block cannot be used, so every view ordered by urgency refuses: {detail}
check.urgency-malformed.context: A check finding: this workbench's dinah.urgency block, which declares the weights of the urgency order, cannot be read, so every view ordered by urgency refuses to draw until it is repaired. {detail} carries `dinah.urgency not-a-mapping`, or the path of the member at fault followed by the machine token malformed-term. dinah.urgency is the key the weights are declared under and is never translated.

check.urgency-member-unknown.text: the dinah.urgency block carries a member this build does not read, and it is ignored: {detail}
check.urgency-member-unknown.context: A check finding at cleanup severity: a member of this workbench's dinah.urgency block that this build does not read, such as a misspelt weight. {detail} carries the member's path within the block, such as age.perday. The member is kept in the file and ignored, so the term it was meant for keeps its default.

check.urgency-level-count.context: A check finding at cleanup severity: the dinah.urgency block declares a priority or severity weight list whose length differs from the number of levels the workbench declares on that axis. {detail} carries the axis, the list's length and the declared count. check.newline-conflict.locked.context: One row of the newline repair's busy report: a file whose lock another process holds, read from the lock's own content. {path} carries the file and {detail} carries the holder.

check.newline-conflict.unreadable.text: {path} will not open, so the run could not read it.
check.newline-conflict.unreadable.context: One row of the newline repair's refusal report: a file the run cannot read, and it will not write a store it has not read whole. {path} carries the file.

check.newline-conflict.unsupported.text: {path} carries something this repair will not decide: {detail}.
check.newline-conflict.unsupported.context: One row of the newline repair's refusal report: a file whose transform refuses it. {path} carries the file and {detail} carries the frontmatter key, the record number, or the words saying that the file does not round-trip through the anchor reader. Deciding what a damaged file or a damaged record should become is a different piece of work from deciding what a line ending should be.

check.newline-conflict.unwritable.text: {path} could not be written, so nothing was written at all.
check.newline-conflict.unwritable.context: One row of the newline repair's refusal report: a destination whose rehearsed write failed, which is what the rehearsal exists to find. {path} carries the file. The rehearsal renames the file's own bytes back over it, so a failure here is the failure the confirmed run would meet.

check.newline-repair-unsupported.text: the newline repair will not decide this file, so it is left exactly as it is ({detail})
check.newline-repair-unsupported.context: A check finding: a workbench text file the newline repair refuses rather than guessing at. {detail} says which case, either that a file bearing one of the anchor names the format fixes does not round-trip through the anchor reader, or the frontmatter key whose shape the repair cannot re-render. Such a file need carry no carriage return at all, which is why this is not reported as a stored line ending; deciding what a damaged header should become is separate work from deciding what a line ending should be.

check.newline-rewrite-loose.one.text: It also carries {count} carriage return that is not a line ending, which the repair leaves alone.
check.newline-rewrite-loose.one.context: The clause drawn under a destination that also carries a carriage return the repair does not touch, for exactly one. A carriage return not followed by a line feed is a character the prose meant to carry rather than a line ending, so it is reported and kept. The line is drawn only where the count is above zero.

check.newline-rewrite-loose.other.text: It also carries {count} carriage returns that are not line endings, which the repair leaves alone.
check.newline-rewrite-loose.other.context: The same clause for any other number.

check.newline-rewrote-file.one.context: One destination a confirmed newline repair wrote, for exactly one stored line ending. It is drawn only for a file the run actually rewrote, so a busy file or one a partial failure did not reach keeps the preview's tense instead.

check.newline-rewrote-file.other.context: One destination a confirmed newline repair wrote, for any other number.

check.newline-would-rewrite-file.one.text: {path} carries {count} stored line ending to repair.
check.newline-would-rewrite-file.one.context: One destination a newline preview found, for exactly one stored line ending. {path} is the file and {count} is what the file's own transform would remove. The tense is the file's rather than the run's, because a confirmed run can carry a destination it did not reach.

check.newline-would-rewrite-file.other.text: {path} carries {count} stored line endings to repair.
check.newline-would-rewrite-file.other.context: One destination a newline preview found, for any other number. A count of zero cannot occur here, because a file with nothing to remove is not a destination.

check.newlines-busy.one.text: {count} file was busy and was not rewritten; run this again to pick it up.
check.newlines-busy.one.context: The line the newline repair prints for one file whose lock another process holds. A held lock is the one condition that does not stop the run: a lock is held for milliseconds, a run takes one per file across thousands of files, and several sessions work a busy workbench at once, so a run refusing over a transient lock would refuse most of the time.

check.newlines-busy.other.text: {count} files were busy and were not rewritten; run this again to pick them up.
check.newlines-busy.other.context: The line the newline repair prints for any other number of files whose locks another process holds.

check.newlines-confirm.context: The line a newline preview prints under what it would repair. It parts company with the two number repairs either side of it, which refuse without confirmation rather than previewing.

check.newlines-examined.one.context: The line the newline repair prints for the size of the set it read, for exactly one file. A sweep says how many files it walked, because a sweep that reports nothing and walked nothing reads the same as a clean store.

check.newlines-examined.other.context: The line the newline repair prints for the size of the set it read, for any other number. A count of zero is a run that found no text file to read, which is that run's own answer.

check.newlines-heading.context: The heading the newline repair prints for a confirmed run, which is the run that writes the repaired bytes.

check.newlines-nothing.context: The line the newline repair prints when no examined file stores a carriage return standing for a line ending. A second run of a repair that succeeded prints this, because the repair is idempotent by construction: a file is a destination exactly when its own transform changes it, and every transform answers bytes it would not change again.

check.newlines-preview.text: Newline migration (preview). Each destination below was rewritten with its own bytes, to prove it can be written; content is unchanged and a destination's modification time is now.
check.newlines-preview.context: The heading the newline repair prints when it was asked for without --yes. It says that the preview writes rather than claiming that nothing was written, because the preview does write: nothing short of performing the rename predicts whether the rename will be permitted, so the only way a preview can promise that the confirmed run will succeed is to rehearse each destination's write with that destination's own bytes.

check.newlines-refused.one.context: The line the newline repair prints when one destination met a condition that stops the whole run, so a preview predicts the outcome instead of a run discovering a refusal half way through.

check.newlines-refused.other.context: The line the newline repair prints for any other number of destinations meeting a condition that stops the whole run.

check.newlines-rewritten.one.context: The line a confirmed newline repair prints for what it wrote, for exactly one file.

check.newlines-rewritten.other.context: The line a confirmed newline repair prints for what it wrote, for any other number.

check.newlines-would-rewrite.one.context: The line a newline preview prints for what it found to repair, for exactly one file.

check.newlines-would-rewrite.other.context: The line a newline preview prints for what it found to repair, for any other number.

check.standing-filing.context: One line of the standing-item repair's own report, naming a card, the column whose declaration minted the instance and the entry key. {card} and {column} carry references and {key} the entry's key, all read off the store, so all three are machine vocabulary and none is translated.

check.standing-item-malformed.text: column {detail} carries a standing entry or a line the reader cannot read, so nothing is minted for it
check.standing-item-malformed.context: A check finding: one entry of a column's standing_items block that the reader refused, which is an entry whose key is outside the one-segment grammar, whose kind is absent or outside the three item kinds, whose text is absent or blank, or a dashed line where a member line was expected. {detail} carries the column's reference and then the key as written, or the offending line. The entry mints nothing and the column still opens, so the repair is an edit to the block.

check.standing-item-missing.text: a card standing in a declaring column carries no instance of a standing item, so the column's hold has nothing to hold on: {detail}
check.standing-item-missing.context: A check finding at cleanup severity. {detail} carries the card's reference, the column's reference and the entry key, in that order. Every card that entered the column before the declaration was written produces one line per missing entry, and `dinah check --file-standing --yes` is the operator's repair, which mints the instances through the path an arrival uses.

check.standing-items-entry-hold.text: column {detail} declares standing items and holds on entry alone; they are minted after the entry hold is read, so they hold no card's first arrival and no departure and hold only a card returning to the column, and dinah set {detail} hold out is the usual fix
check.standing-items-entry-hold.context: A check finding at cleanup severity. {detail} is the column's reference. A column whose gate_items reads true declares standing items that are enforced only on a card that has already been through, which is unlikely to be what its author meant; a column at out, both or off is not reported.

check.standing-preview.text: Nothing was written, because this run carried no confirmation.
check.standing-preview.context: The first line the standing-item repair prints when it ran without the confirmation flag, so that a reader cannot take the lines below it for work that happened.

check.standing-would-file.one.context: The line the standing-item repair's preview prints, for exactly one instance a confirmed run would mint.

check.standing-would-file.other.context: The line the standing-item repair's preview prints, for any count of instances a confirmed run would mint other than one, including none.

check.standing-would-filing.context: One line of the standing-item repair's preview, naming a card, the column whose declaration would mint the instance and the entry key. It is spelled apart from check.standing-filing because a preview writes nothing, and the same sentence under both would tell an operator a write had happened. {card} and {column} carry references and {key} the entry's key, all read off the store, so none is translated.

check.stored-carriage-return.text: this file stores a carriage return that stands for a line ending ({detail})
check.stored-carriage-return.context: A check finding: a workbench text file carrying a carriage return the format's Encoding section forbids a writer to produce. {detail} carries the count the file's own transform would remove and, separately, the count of carriage returns that are not line endings, because the second number is legal and the first is not. The counts come from the transform rather than from a pattern search, so this finding and dinah check --migrate-newlines can never disagree about which files are dirty.

check.stranded-column.text: the workbench names a column whose directory is not there ({detail}); dinah check --migrate-columns removes it from the list
check.stranded-column.context: A check finding: a column a retiring act moved or removed without also editing the definition, or one removed by hand; the path carried is the workbench anchor rather than a per-column file, since there is no per-column file left to point at.

check.tier-without-models.text: this workbench declares tier {detail} and its tiers table lists no model for it
check.tier-without-models.context: A check finding: every member of levels.tier that a tiers table exists for is listed with at least one model. {detail} is the tier's own name. A tier nothing satisfies strands every card that asks for it, so a rung nobody runs a model at is a rung to drop from levels.tier rather than one to leave empty.

check.tiers-entry-malformed.text: an entry of the tiers table does not read: {detail}
check.tiers-entry-malformed.context: A check finding: every entry of the tiers table carries a meaning, a models sequence, and model entries written as one flow mapping of provider, model and an optional server. {detail} carries the tier and then the line, in that order. The reader skips such an entry rather than refusing the workbench, so this is where a person meets the damage.

check.vocabulary-confirm.text: Nothing was written. The preview reads the format each workbench declares and does not open it, so a workbench listed above can still be refused by the run that carries it. Run the same command again with --yes to carry these workbenches across the rename.

check.vocabulary-failed.other.context: The heading over the workbenches the vocabulary migration met an error on, for any other number.

check.vocabulary-malformed.other.text: {count} workbenches declare no profile this build can read, and were left alone.
check.vocabulary-malformed.other.context: The heading over the candidates the vocabulary migration could not classify, for any other number.

check.workbench-slug-assigned.context: The line the workbench-slug migration prints for what it derived, once, since a run repairs at most one workbench.

check.workbench-slug-malformed.text: the workbench carries the slug {detail}, and a workbench slug is a letter followed by letters, digits, and single interior dashes, with at least one letter in its last segment
check.workbench-slug-malformed.context: A check finding: the workbench's stored slug does not match the workbench slug grammar, so nobody can rely on typing it. Open validates the stored slug at no major, so the workbench still opens while this is reported.

check.workbench-slug-missing.text: the workbench carries no slug, so its cards are reachable only by their identifiers
check.workbench-slug-missing.context: A check finding: a workbench written before the workbench-level slug field existed; `dinah check --migrate-slugs` derives one from the title.

check.workbench-slug-underivable.text: the workbench carries a title no slug can be derived from, so the migration gave it none
check.workbench-slug-underivable.context: A check finding the workbench-slug migration raises: no letter of the workbench's title survives the derivation, so a person retitles the workbench or writes a slug onto its anchor by hand.

check.workbench.1.text: the workbench declares a profile version the tool implements
check.workbench.1.context: One row of the ordered precondition list of workbench, quoted from section 6 of the core profile.

check.workbench.2.context: One row of the ordered precondition list of workbench, quoted from section 6 of the core profile.

check.workstream-slug-duplicate.context: A check finding: two workstreams share a slug, which leaves a reference with two answers; a person picks which one changes.

check.workstream-slug-malformed.text: workstream {detail} carries a slug that is not a letter followed by letters, digits, and single interior dashes
check.workstream-slug-malformed.context: A check finding: a workstream's stored slug does not match the slug grammar, so nobody can rely on typing it.

check.workstream-slug-missing.text: workstream {detail} carries no slug, so it is reachable only by its identifier
check.workstream-slug-missing.context: A check finding: a workstream carrying no slug, which is what an adopted workstream and a hand-written one both start as; `dinah check --migrate-slugs` derives one from the title.

check.workstream-slug-underivable.text: workstream {detail} carries a title no slug can be derived from, so the migration gave it none
check.workstream-slug-underivable.context: A check finding the slug migration raises: no letter of the workstream's title survives the derivation, or it carries no title at all, so a person names it and runs the migration again.

check.workstream-slug-unwritable.text: workstream {detail} could not be written to, so the migration gave it no slug and carried on
check.workstream-slug-unwritable.context: A check finding the slug migration raises: the workstream's anchor could not be read or written, the walk stepped over it and carried on.

contents.archived.text: These addresses resolve once {ref} is restored.
contents.archived.context: The line printed under the heading of `dinah list --archived`, once per listing. The rows below it carry the addresses the walk's children will have when the root is restored, and none of them resolves while the root is archived. {ref} is the root's own reference, an address rather than prose, and no word may agree with it.

contents.empty.context: Printed when `dinah list` is asked about an entity with nothing below it. No table follows, and the call succeeds: an entity that contains nothing is an answer rather than a mistake.

contents.empty.collection.context: Printed when `dinah list` is asked about a collection with no members. No table follows and the call succeeds, for the reason contents.empty gives for an entity.

contents.header.context: The sentence above the tree `dinah list` prints, naming the entity the walk started from. {count} is how many entities sit below it, at every depth and not only the ones drawn.

contents.header.collection.context: The sentence above the tree `dinah list` prints when the reference names a whole collection rather than one entity. A collection has no title of its own, so it is named by the reference alone, and {count} is how many entities sit below it at every depth rather than only the ones drawn.
