help.group.workbench.context: A heading of the help block, grouping the commands beneath it.

help.guide.context: The closing line of a command's help page, pointing at the guide that explains that command's argument language. {topic} is the guide's topic name, which is machine vocabulary and is never translated.

help.reading.text: Run 'dinah guide' for the guides Dinah carries, and read the quick start at https://github.com/paulmooreparks/dinah/blob/main/docs/quick-start.md
help.reading.context: The line below the help block's footer, pointing a reader at the guides the binary carries and at the quick start. The URL names a location rather than reading as prose, and it stays as it is in every language.

help.reference-kinds.context: One argument's meaning followed by the kinds of thing its reference may name. {summary} is the argument's own sentence. {kinds} holds the labels reference.kind.workbench, reference.kind.workstream, reference.kind.column, reference.kind.card, reference.kind.below-card and reference.kind.collection, joined by a semicolon and a space, and those labels are translated prose rather than machine vocabulary, so unlike {kind} in the unknown-field refusals a word of this sentence may agree with what is substituted here. No label may itself contain a semicolon followed by a space, because the guard over this clause splits the list on that pair.

help.refusals.text: What can go wrong, in the order each is checked:
help.refusals.context: The heading above a command's ordered precondition list in its own help.

help.tagline.context: The first line of the help block, the tool's one-sentence description. The word Dinah names the product and stays in Latin script; do not respell it.

help.usage.context: The usage line. The word dinah and the bracketed placeholders are syntax and stay as they are.

help.vocabulary.context: One argument's meaning followed by the closed set of values it accepts. {summary} is the argument's own sentence and {values} is the members separated by commas. The members are machine vocabulary and are never translated.

init.actor.recorded.text: Dinah recorded you as actor {actor} in {path}, and will record that name on everything you do. Run `dinah config set actor <name>` to change it, or `dinah config set actor` to clear it.
init.actor.recorded.context: Printed after init records the actor in the person's own configuration. Dinah records it only when no flag, variable or setting already named an actor. {actor} is the name recorded and {path} is the file it was written to. The word Dinah names the product and stays in Latin script; do not respell it. The command text is typed literally and stays as it is.

init.actor.unrecorded.text: Dinah created the workbench but could not record you as actor in {path} ({reason}). Run `dinah config set actor <name>` to say who you are.
init.actor.unrecorded.context: Printed after init creates the workbench and then fails to write the person's own configuration. The workbench exists, so this is a report rather than a refusal and carries no refusal name. {path} is the file Dinah tried to write and {reason} is the cause, which arrives in English from the operating system. The word Dinah names the product and stays in Latin script; do not respell it. The command text is typed literally and stays as it is.

instructions.column.context: The label above the column's own instructions.

instructions.column-attachments.context: The label above the listing of the column's own attachments, served after the column's instructions.

instructions.column-attachments.read.text: Read one with `dinah path`, naming its reference followed by `/payload`.
instructions.column-attachments.read.context: Printed under the listing of the column's attachments. `dinah path` and `/payload` are typed literally and are not translated; the reference is one from the Ref column of the listing above.

instructions.global.context: The label above the user-global instruction layer.

instructions.loop.context: The line served with the instructions where the card's column declares a loop_limit. {count} is how often this card has already left that column backwards, {limit} is what the column declares, and {column} names the column.

instructions.moves.context: The label above the legal moves served with the instructions.

instructions.standing.context: The label above the workbench's standing instructions.

listing-comments.empty.context: Printed when dinah list <card>/comments is asked about a card that carries no comments. No table follows, and the call succeeds: a card with nothing to say is an answer rather than a mistake.

listing-comments.header.context: The sentence above the table dinah list <card>/comments prints, naming the collection the reader asked about. {count} is how many comments the card carries.

listing-items.empty.context: Printed when dinah list <card>/checklist is asked about a card that carries no checklist items. No table follows, and the call succeeds: a card with nothing on its checklist is an answer rather than a mistake.

listing-items.header.context: The sentence above the table dinah list <card>/checklist prints, naming the collection the reader asked about. {count} is how many checklist items the card carries.

log.attachment-renamed.context: The detail of a recorded attachment_renamed, carrying the old filename as {from} and the new filename as {to}.

log.item-filed.standing.context: The detail of an item_filed line a column's standing declaration wrote: the declaring column and the entry key. {column} is the title the event captured at write time, falling back to the stored identifier on a line that captured none, and {key} is the entry's key, which is machine vocabulary and is never translated. A hand filing's line carries no standing key and draws no detail.

log.manual-correction.text: {from} to {to}, recorded from a hand edit
log.manual-correction.context: The detail of a witnessed correction, carrying the column the journal believed and the column the anchor records. It reads differently from a move because nobody chose this transition; the tool found it.

log.moved.context: The detail of a recorded move, carrying the titles as they stood at the time.

log.override.context: The mark on a move admitted under an operator's override.

log.reject.context: The mark on a move whose destination is the departure column's own reject_to target.

log.renumbered.context: The detail of a recorded renumbered, carrying the number the card arrived holding as {from} and the number the repair gave it as {to}.

log.tier-overridden.context: The detail of a tier_overridden line: the column the override concerns, and the requirement on either side of the write. {column} is the title the event captured at write time, falling back to the stored identifier on a line that captured none. {from} is the previous requirement, or log.tier-overridden.no-requirement where the card asked for nothing. log.tier-overridden.reason is appended after this one only when the event carries a reason, which an ordinary `set <ref> tier <value> --at <column>` write does not.

log.tier-overridden.no-requirement.context: Spliced in as {from} on a tier_overridden line whose own from is empty, meaning the card asked for nothing at this column before the write.

log.tier-overridden.reason.context: Appended to log.tier-overridden's detail when the event carries a reason, which today only a raise writes. It is a parenthesis around the prose and nothing else, which is why every catalog answers it the same way.

lsp.completion.card.detail.context: The detail line beside one card candidate in a completion list. {column} is the title of the column the card stands in and {state} is its condition.

lsp.completion.column.detail.context: The detail line beside one column candidate in a completion list. {slug} is the column's own handle and {position} is its one-based place in the flow.

lsp.completion.workstream.detail.context: The detail line beside one workstream candidate in a completion list. {slug} is the workstream's own handle.

lsp.hover.workbench.context: The last line of every hover the language server answers, so a reader with two repositories open knows which workbench answered. {workbench} is the workbench's title.

lsp.label.attachment.context: The inline annotation and hover line for an attachment reference. {filename} is the payload's original name.

lsp.label.card.context: The inline annotation and hover line for a card reference with no holder. {title} is the card's title and {column} is the title of the column it stands in.

lsp.label.card.held.context: The inline annotation and hover line for a card somebody is holding. {holder} is the owner name recorded on the claim.

lsp.label.column.context: The inline annotation and hover line for a column that holds a card neither on the way in nor on the way out. {title} is the column's title.

lsp.label.column.holds-both.context: The inline annotation and hover line for a column that holds a card on the way in and on the way out.

lsp.label.column.holds-in.context: The inline annotation and hover line for a column that holds a card on the way in while an item naming it is unresolved.

lsp.label.column.holds-out.context: The inline annotation and hover line for a column that holds a card on the way out while an item naming it is unresolved.

lsp.label.item.context: The inline annotation and hover line for a checklist item naming no owner. {kind} and {state} are canonical tokens spliced untranslated, such as open_question and pending.

lsp.label.item.owned.context: The inline annotation and hover line for a checklist item that names an owner. {kind} and {state} are canonical tokens spliced untranslated; {owner} is the owner name.

lsp.label.unresolved.context: The inline annotation and hover line for a value at a declared front-matter reference position that resolves to no entity. It is a report of what the value names and not a diagnostic.

lsp.label.workstream.context: The inline annotation and hover line for a workstream reference. {title} is the workstream's title.

lsp.log.no-refresh-support.text: this editor declared no inlay-hint refresh support, so an inline annotation will not update until its document is edited or reopened
lsp.log.no-refresh-support.context: The line the language server writes to the editor's log once at startup when the client declared no inlay-hint refresh support. It tells a reader why a label may go stale, rather than leaving them to conclude the annotation lies.

lsp.log.slow-walk.entered.text: the workbench walk took {duration} against a poll interval of {interval}, so refresh latency is now bounded by the walk rather than by the interval
lsp.log.slow-walk.entered.context: The warning the language server writes to the editor's log on entering the state where a change walk outruns the poll interval. {duration} is the measured walk and {interval} is the interval it outran. It is sent once on the edge and never once per tick.

lsp.log.slow-walk.left.text: the workbench walk took {duration} against a poll interval of {interval}, so refresh latency is back at the interval
lsp.log.slow-walk.left.context: The warning the language server writes to the editor's log on leaving the state where a change walk outruns the poll interval. {duration} is the walk that left the state and {interval} is the interval the loop is again sleeping.

lsp.log.workbench.context: The line the language server writes to the editor's log once at startup, naming which workbench answered. {root} is that workbench's directory.

lsp.no-workbench.text: Dinah found no workbench here, so nothing is annotated yet
lsp.no-workbench.context: The one message the language server shows a reader when no workbench resolved at startup. The server keeps serving and retries on every poll, so this says what is missing rather than reporting a failure.

mcp.no-default.context: The one line dinah mcp writes to stderr when startup discovery resolved a workbench the root does not contain or the ancestor walk found none, and a later call has to be told no default will answer.

mcp.reach.text: You may reach any workbench under {root}; this server is serving {title} by default. The workbenches tool lists the workbenches under the root, and the workbench property on any other tool names one.
mcp.reach.context: The third paragraph of the working agreement when the server has a default workbench. {root} is the directory --root or DINAH_MCP_ROOT named, and {title} is the default workbench's own title.

mcp.reach.nodefault.text: You may reach any workbench under {root}; this server is serving no default. The workbenches tool lists the workbenches under the root, and the workbench property on any other tool names one.
mcp.reach.nodefault.context: The third paragraph of the working agreement when the server has no default workbench. {root} is the directory --root or DINAH_MCP_ROOT named.

mcp.reach.nodefault.unbounded.text: You may reach any workbench you can name; this server was given no root and is serving no default. The workbenches tool needs a root to search and refuses dinah.no-workbench-found here, so name the one you want directly on the workbench property of any other tool.
mcp.reach.nodefault.unbounded.context: The third paragraph of the working agreement when the server has no default workbench and no root: --root and DINAH_MCP_ROOT were both empty and discovery found nothing, so PathUnderRoot admits every candidate and only the checks made when the workbench is opened can refuse one.

mcp.reach.unbounded.text: You may reach any workbench you can name; this server was given no root and is serving {title} by default. The workbenches tool needs a root to search, so a call naming no path answers only the default it is serving, with unbounded set on the response rather than as a search result; name the workbench you want directly on the workbench property of any other tool, or leave it unnamed to use the default.
mcp.reach.unbounded.context: The third paragraph of the working agreement when the server has a default workbench but no root: --root and DINAH_MCP_ROOT were both empty, discovery found a workbench to serve as default, and the auto-narrowing that used to bind root to that workbench's own directory (dinah-307) no longer runs, so PathUnderRoot admits every other candidate too. {title} is the default workbench's own title. The workbenches tool still cannot search an empty root, so a call naming no path answers the one candidate it already knows, the default, marked unbounded rather than presented as a completed search (dinah-301); it no longer refuses dinah.no-workbench-found in this one combination, though it still does when there is no default to fall back on.

next.above-tier.context: Printed beside a column that offers no card because the tier the caller declared is admitted for none of the work standing there, in place of next.none, which says only that nothing is ready.

next.awaiting-outside.context: Printed beside a column that offers no card because it waits on somebody outside the workbench, in place of next.none, which says only that nothing is ready.

next.no-taker.context: Printed beside a column that offers no card because no act could take one up from there, in place of next.none, which says only that nothing is ready. A done column holding four ready cards prints this one.

next.none.context: Printed beside a column offering no card.

next.take.claim.context: The value under the offers listing's Take column on a card an owner takes up where it stands. It names the command a reader types, so it reads as the act rather than as a sentence about it.

next.take.pull.context: The value under the offers listing's Take column on a card that leaves by a pull into the column beyond, because nobody takes work up where it stands. It names the command a reader types.

outcome.stale.text: the card moved since you read it; its revision is now {revision}
outcome.stale.context: The sentence after the stale outcome name. {revision} is the card's current revision.

outcome.unreachable.text: the question could not be asked: {detail}
outcome.unreachable.context: The sentence after the unreachable outcome name.

param.add.column.summary.text: which column to file the card in; the first column when you name none
param.add.column.summary.context: The meaning of the column argument of `dinah add`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.add.priority.summary.text: which priority level to file the card with, from the levels this workbench declares
param.add.priority.summary.context: The meaning of the priority argument of `dinah add`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.add.severity.summary.text: which severity level to file the card with, from the levels this workbench declares
param.add.severity.summary.context: The meaning of the severity argument of `dinah add`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.add.title.summary.text: the card's title, in one shell word or in quotation marks
param.add.title.summary.context: The meaning of the title argument of `dinah add`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.archived.summary.text: resolve the reference in the archive rather than in the live set
param.archived.summary.context: The meaning of the --archived flag, shared by restore, show, path and contents, printed in each command's arguments table. On those four the flag names one half rather than widening: the reference resolves against the archive mirror at its deepest collection step. The same flag on `dinah search` widens the scan instead and carries its own sentence under param.search.archived.summary.

param.attach.description.summary.text: a line describing the attachment, stored beside it
param.attach.description.summary.context: The meaning of the description argument of `dinah attach`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.attach.file.summary.text: a path on this machine to the file you are attaching
param.attach.file.summary.context: The meaning of the file argument of `dinah attach`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.attach.ref.summary.text: what the file hangs off; below a card that is a comment, or, with --replace, the attachment whose bytes you are replacing
param.attach.ref.summary.context: The meaning of the ref argument of `dinah attach`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.attach.replace.summary.text: replace an existing attachment's bytes instead of adding one
param.attach.replace.summary.context: The meaning of the replace argument of `dinah attach`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.block.card.summary.context: The meaning of the card argument of `dinah block`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.block.kind.summary.text: your own word for what sort of obstacle this is; Dinah stores whatever you write and checks it against no set
param.block.kind.summary.context: The meaning of the kind argument of `dinah block`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.block.reason.summary.text: why it is blocked, in one shell word or in quotation marks
param.block.reason.summary.context: The meaning of the reason argument of `dinah block`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.card.summary.text: the card you are acting on, written as its reference, such as wb-1
param.card.summary.context: The meaning of the card argument, shared by every command that takes a card and nothing else.

param.changes.column.summary.text: which column to report about, also written --column <column>; every column when you name none
param.changes.column.summary.context: The meaning of the column argument of `dinah changes`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.changes.since.summary.text: the cursor a previous run printed; a run naming none mints one and reports nothing
param.changes.since.summary.context: The meaning of the since argument of `dinah changes`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.changes.timeout.summary.text: how long a waiting call blocks, written as a number and a unit: 30m, 2h, 7d; it blocks until the cursor advances when you write none
param.changes.timeout.summary.context: The meaning of the --timeout flag of `dinah changes`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.changes.wait.summary.text: hold the call open until the cursor advances or --timeout lapses, instead of answering immediately
param.changes.wait.summary.context: The meaning of the --wait flag of `dinah changes`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.check.file-standing.summary.text: mint, on every card standing in a column declaring standing items, the instances it is missing; without --yes it reports what it would file and writes nothing
param.check.file-standing.summary.context: The meaning of the file-standing argument of `dinah check`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.check.finish.summary.text: complete or roll back a structural act that was interrupted
param.check.finish.summary.context: The meaning of the finish argument of `dinah check`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.check.force-claims.summary.text: carries the conversion past a card somebody still holds, naming every such card in the workbench's own history
param.check.force-claims.summary.context: The written meaning of the --force-claims flag of check, which is the workbench operator's own way past a claim nobody can release.

param.check.migrate-applies-when.summary.text: stamps the workbench with the format that declares applies_when conditions and the mapping form of a level axis, from any lower number, so that an older Dinah refuses the store instead of misreading it; it converts no designation, so a workbench below format 7 runs --migrate-designations first; without --yes it writes nothing
param.check.migrate-applies-when.summary.context: The written meaning of the --migrate-applies-when flag of check. It writes the one format line on the workbench anchor and reads no card, and without the confirmation flag it writes nothing at all.

param.check.migrate-branches.summary.text: lift the retired heading out of every card body into a declared field and stamp this store's format
param.check.migrate-branches.summary.context: The meaning of the migrate-branches argument of `dinah check`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.check.migrate-columns.summary.text: remove stranded identifiers from this workbench's own list of columns
param.check.migrate-columns.summary.context: The meaning of the migrate-columns argument of `dinah check`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.check.migrate-container.summary.text: carry this workbench into a .dinah container under an identifier Dinah minted, or every workbench beneath --root
param.check.migrate-container.summary.context: The one-line summary of the check command flag --migrate-container, printed by `dinah help check`.

param.check.migrate-designations.summary.text: converts every checklist item's answer from a position to the designated comment's own identifier, and stamps the workbench with the format that declares it
param.check.migrate-designations.summary.context: The written meaning of the --migrate-designations flag of check. It is the workbench operator's own act and is refused while any card is held.

param.check.migrate-newlines.summary.text: repair every text file storing a carriage return that stands for a line ending, rewriting each destination with its own bytes first to prove it can be written; an interrupted run may leave a .dinah-* file beside an anchor, which is safe to delete because nothing reads it
param.check.migrate-newlines.summary.context: The meaning of the migrate-newlines argument of `dinah check`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.check.migrate-numbers.summary.text: build the card-number registry from the numbers this workbench's cards still carry
param.check.migrate-numbers.summary.context: The meaning of the migrate-numbers argument of `dinah check`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.check.migrate-ordinals.summary.text: stamp a creation ordinal on every entity that carries none
param.check.migrate-ordinals.summary.context: The meaning of the migrate-ordinals argument of `dinah check`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.check.migrate-slugs.summary.text: derive a slug for every column of this workbench that carries none
param.check.migrate-slugs.summary.context: The meaning of the migrate-slugs argument of `dinah check`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.check.migrate-vocabulary.summary.text: carry this workbench across the column and state rename, or every workbench beneath --root
param.check.migrate-vocabulary.summary.context: The meaning of the migrate-vocabulary argument of `dinah check`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.check.migrate-workstreams.summary.text: adopt every workstream a card names that this workbench does not carry
param.check.migrate-workstreams.summary.context: The meaning of the migrate-workstreams argument of `dinah check`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.check.rehearse.summary.text: decides the conversion by the same rules, prints the same report, and writes nothing at all
param.check.rehearse.summary.context: The written meaning of the --rehearse flag of check, which turns the designation conversion into a rehearsal.

param.check.remint.summary.text: give the workbench at this path a fresh identifier
param.check.remint.summary.context: The one-line summary of the check command flag --remint, printed by `dinah help check`. The flag takes one directory path.

param.check.renumber.summary.text: move every later claimant when two cards arrive holding one number
param.check.renumber.summary.context: The meaning of the renumber argument of `dinah check`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.check.witness.summary.text: record a manual correction on every card whose position was edited by hand
param.check.witness.summary.context: The meaning of the witness argument of `dinah check`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.cite.item.summary.text: the checklist item the citation is added to, such as wb-1/criteria/1
param.cite.item.summary.context: The written meaning of cite's item argument. wb-1 stands for a card reference and is not translated.

param.cite.observed.summary.text: what the check showed before the work and after it, written fail:pass
param.cite.observed.summary.context: The written meaning of cite's observed flag. Each half is fail or pass, and both words are machine vocabulary that is never translated.

param.cite.scheme.summary.text: the evidence scheme the citation draws on, as the workbench declares it
param.cite.scheme.summary.context: The written meaning of cite's scheme argument. Dinah writes the scheme down as given, and dinah check is what reports one the workbench never declared.

param.cite.target.summary.text: what that scheme points at, such as a test path or an attachment identifier
param.cite.target.summary.context: The written meaning of cite's target argument.

param.claim.card.summary.text: the card you are taking up
param.claim.card.summary.context: The meaning of the card argument of `dinah claim`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.claim.expires.summary.text: how long your claim holds before it goes stale, written as a number and a unit: 30m, 2h, 7d
param.claim.expires.summary.context: The meaning of the expires argument of `dinah claim`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.column.action.summary.text: create a column; new is the only action this build carries
param.column.action.summary.context: The meaning of the action argument of `dinah column`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.column.before.summary.text: the column the new one is placed immediately ahead of, appended to the end of the flow when you say nothing
param.column.before.summary.context: The meaning of the before argument of `dinah column`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.column.capacity.summary.text: the most cards the new column holds at once, unlimited when you say nothing
param.column.capacity.summary.context: The meaning of the capacity argument of `dinah column`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.column.column.summary.text: the title of the column you are creating
param.column.column.summary.context: The meaning of the title argument of `dinah column`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.column.kind.summary.text: which kind the new column carries: intake, work, done, or dinah.buffer; work when you say nothing
param.column.kind.summary.context: The meaning of the kind argument of `dinah column`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.column.slug.summary.text: the short handle you type instead of quoting the title, derived from the title when you say nothing
param.column.slug.summary.context: The meaning of the slug argument of `dinah column`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.column.tier.summary.text: the tier the work here usually needs; it informs a relative card write and never refuses a claim, so it cannot make this column selective
param.column.tier.summary.context: The meaning of the tier argument of `dinah column`, printed in that command's arguments table. The second clause is the limit a caller has to meet before relying on the field: only a requirement a card carries can refuse a claim, so a station is protected one card at a time and never by its own default.

param.comment.card.summary.text: the card, the column or the checklist item you are commenting on, written as its reference, such as wb-1, triage or wb-1/questions/2
param.comment.card.summary.context: The meaning of comment's own card argument, which comment no longer shares with the plain-card commands because it also takes a column and a checklist item below a card.

param.comment.text.summary.text: the comment, in one shell word or in quotation marks; a single - reads it from a pipe
param.comment.text.summary.context: The meaning of the text argument of `dinah comment`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.config.action.summary.text: read one setting or write one; every setting with its value when you name none
param.config.action.summary.context: The meaning of the action argument of `dinah config`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.config.key.summary.text: which setting you are reading or writing
param.config.key.summary.context: The meaning of the key argument of `dinah config`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.config.value.summary.text: what to store under it, on a set
param.config.value.summary.context: The meaning of the value argument of `dinah config`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.edit.card.summary.text: the thing you are opening in your editor, such as wb-1/comments/1
param.edit.card.summary.context: The meaning of the card argument of `dinah edit`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.extract.dir.summary.text: where to write this workbench's definition
param.extract.dir.summary.context: The meaning of the dir argument of `dinah extract`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.file.column.summary.text: the column the item names, written on the item only when you give one
param.file.column.summary.context: The written meaning of file's column flag. It says the field is absent when the flag is absent. The value has to name a column the workbench declares, because file resolves the reference to that column's identifier and a column gate matches on the identifier.

param.file.kind.summary.text: the kind of judgement being recorded: acceptance_criterion, open_question or decision
param.file.kind.summary.context: The written meaning of file's kind argument. The three kind names are machine vocabulary and are never translated.

param.file.owner.summary.text: who the item is meant for; on an item whose owner reads operator, resolve, verify and fail are refused to anybody but the operator
param.file.owner.summary.context: The written meaning of file's owner flag. It states what the tool refuses: on an item whose owner reads operator, resolve, verify and fail are refused not-operator to every actor but the workbench's operator, and so is a write to that item's own owner key.

param.file.text.summary.text: the item's own text, in one shell word or in quotation marks; a single - reads it from a pipe
param.file.text.summary.context: The written meaning of file's text argument.

param.get.field.summary.context: The meaning of the field argument of `dinah get`, printed in that command's arguments table. The set the argument publishes is the union over every kind, and the refusal names the resolved kind's own set.

param.init.slug.summary.text: the prefix every card reference carries; derived from the directory's name when you name none

param.lsp.poll-seconds.summary.text: how often the server rereads the workbench for a change; 2 when you name none
param.lsp.poll-seconds.summary.context: The meaning of the --poll-seconds argument of `dinah lsp`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.lsp.root.summary.text: directory the workbench this server serves lies under; the workbench discovered at startup when you name none

param.move.override.summary.context: The meaning of the override argument of `dinah move`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.pull.column.summary.context: The meaning of the column argument of `dinah pull`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.raise.tier.summary.context: The meaning of the tier argument of `dinah raise`, printed in that command's arguments table. It resolves the way any tier write resolves, so a relative step is measured against the column's own default and an absolute name is checked against the declared set.

param.ref.summary.text: the entity you are acting on, written as its reference, such as wb-1/comments/1
param.ref.summary.context: The meaning of the ref argument of archive, restore and delete, which take the same set of things.

param.rename.ref.summary.context: The meaning of the ref argument of `dinah rename`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.reopen.reason.summary.text: why the item is being opened again, in one shell word or in quotation marks
param.reopen.reason.summary.context: The written meaning of reopen's reason argument.

param.revoke.permission.summary.text: which standing authorization to take back, written as criterion-retirement
param.revoke.permission.summary.context: The written meaning of the permission argument of revoke. criterion-retirement is machine vocabulary and is never translated.

param.set.at.summary.context: The meaning of the at argument of `dinah set`, printed in that command's arguments table. Every other field takes one value for the whole entity, so naming a column beside one is a usage error.

param.set.field.summary.text: which field you are writing; which names are legal depends on the kind the reference resolves to
param.set.field.summary.context: The meaning of the field argument of `dinah set`, printed in that command's arguments table. The set the argument publishes is the union over every kind, and the refusal names the resolved kind's own set.

param.set.note.summary.text: the note the verb behind a `state` write records; `state` is the one field that takes it
param.set.note.summary.context: The meaning of the note argument of `dinah set`, printed in that command's arguments table. A state write routes to the checklist verb that lands that state, and that verb records a note, so this is where the note is given.

param.set.ref.summary.text: the entity you are writing, written as its reference
param.set.ref.summary.context: The meaning of the ref argument of `dinah set`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.set.value.summary.text: what to store in it; write a single dash to read it from standard input, and leave it out to clear a field that may be cleared
param.set.value.summary.context: The meaning of the value argument of `dinah set`, printed in that command's arguments table. The dash is the spelling `dinah comment` already uses, and it is what sends the several lines a prose field holds.

param.settle.reason.summary.text: why a closed item is being reopened, required when state is pending and read nowhere else
param.settle.reason.summary.context: The written meaning of settle's reason argument, read only when state is pending, which is when settle becomes reopen.

param.settle.state.summary.text: which state the item lands at: resolved or a decision an open question is settled at, verified or failed for an acceptance criterion, or pending to reopen it
param.settle.state.summary.context: The written meaning of settle's state argument, the one word this command adds beyond what resolve, verify, fail and reopen already take.

param.show.card.summary.text: the thing whose detail you are reading, such as wb-1 or wb-1/comments/1
param.show.card.summary.context: The meaning of the card argument of `dinah show`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.show.fields.summary.text: which members of the card the answer carries, written as a comma-separated list; card, body, links and attachments when you name none, with the comments and the checklist served as indexes, and a name ending in .full served with that collection's bodies
param.show.fields.summary.context: The meaning of the fields argument of `dinah show`, printed in that command's arguments table. The table appends the closed set of names a caller may write after this sentence, read off the tool, so the sentence does not spell the set itself.

param.show.all.summary.context: The meaning of the all argument of `dinah show`, printed in that command's arguments table. It is the flag that restores the whole-card answer show gave before the narrow default, and it is refused together with --fields.

param.show.since.summary.text: serve the bodies of the comments after this one-based ordinal, and the index alone for the rest
param.show.since.summary.context: The meaning of the since argument of `dinah show`, printed in that command's arguments table. The word is spelled as it is on `dinah changes`, and this sentence is where the two part: that one takes an opaque cursor and this one takes a comment's position.

param.show.unresolved.summary.text: serve only the checklist items whose state does not release a column hold, which are the pending items, the failed ones, and any item whose state the format does not declare
param.show.unresolved.summary.context: The meaning of the unresolved argument of `dinah show`, printed in that command's arguments table. The state words it stands over are machine vocabulary a reader meets on the item itself.

param.tree.depth.summary.context: The meaning of the depth argument of `dinah tree`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.tree.group-by.summary.context: The meaning of the group-by argument of `dinah tree`, printed in that command's arguments table. The axis names themselves are machine vocabulary and are never translated.

param.tree.query.summary.text: which cards to nest, written as a query in one shell word or in quotation marks; every live card when you write none
param.tree.query.summary.context: The meaning of the query argument of `dinah tree`, printed in that command's arguments table. tree reads the same query language `dinah query` reads.

param.view.view.summary.context: The meaning of the view argument of `dinah view`, printed in that command's arguments table. The argument is a view's name.

param.view.card.summary.context: The meaning of the optional card argument of `dinah view`, printed in that command's arguments table. The argument is a card reference, and the view then draws that card's row alone.

param.view.explain.summary.text: print every term behind each rank of a view ordered by urgency
param.view.explain.summary.context: The meaning of the --explain flag of `dinah view`, printed in that command's arguments table. It prints the arithmetic behind each card's rank, term by term.

param.view.all.summary.context: The meaning of the --all flag of `dinah view`, printed in that command's arguments table. The columns layout draws at most five cards in each column and counts the rest; this flag draws them all. It has no effect on the list layout.

param.view.plain.summary.context: The meaning of the --plain flag of `dinah view`, printed in that command's arguments table. The columns layout normally draws card states, the operator mark and its rules with Unicode symbols; this flag draws them with ASCII characters instead.

param.view.watch.summary.text: draw the view again each time the workbench changes, until Ctrl+C stops it
param.view.watch.summary.context: The meaning of the --watch flag of `dinah view`, printed in that command's arguments table. Ctrl+C is the key a person presses to stop the command; write it the way keyboards in the language label that key.

param.unblock.reason.summary.text: why the block is lifted, in one shell word or in quotation marks; leave it out to lift the block without saying why
param.unblock.reason.summary.context: The meaning of the optional reason argument of `dinah unblock`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.version.catalogs.summary.text: report every shipped language and how much of each is translated
param.version.catalogs.summary.context: The meaning of the catalogs argument of `dinah version`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.workstream.action.summary.text: create a workstream, written as new
param.workstream.action.summary.context: The meaning of the action argument of `dinah list workstreams`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.workstream.slug.summary.text: which slug to create the workstream with, in place of one derived from its title

param.workstream.summary.text: the workstream you are naming, written as its slug or its identifier
param.workstream.summary.context: The meaning of the workstream argument, shared by the commands that name one.

param.workstream.workstream.summary.text: the title of the workstream you are creating
param.workstream.workstream.summary.context: The meaning of the workstream argument of `dinah list workstreams`, printed in that command's arguments table.

param.yes.summary.context: The meaning of the --yes flag, shared by the commands that ask before they destroy something.

query.empty.context: Printed when a query selected no card at all. The query itself was legal, so this is an answer rather than a refusal.

queue.cell.inapplicable.context: The mark the list table prints in a severity or priority cell when that axis does not apply to the card and the card stores nothing there. It stands in a narrow column, so the shortest spelling the language has for not applicable is wanted.

queue.empty.context: Printed when a listing has nothing in it.

reference.kind.below-card.context: One address kind a command's reference may name, printed in the list beside that argument on the command's help page and in the tool schema. No label may itself contain a semicolon followed by a space, because the guard over that list splits it on that pair.

reference.kind.card.context: One address kind a command's reference may name, printed in the list beside that argument on the command's help page and in the tool schema. No label may itself contain a semicolon followed by a space, because the guard over that list splits it on that pair.

reference.kind.collection.context: One address kind a command's reference may name, printed in the list beside that argument on the command's help page and in the tool schema. No label may itself contain a semicolon followed by a space, because the guard over that list splits it on that pair.

reference.kind.column.context: One address kind a command's reference may name, printed in the list beside that argument on the command's help page and in the tool schema. No label may itself contain a semicolon followed by a space, because the guard over that list splits it on that pair.

reference.kind.workbench.context: One address kind a command's reference may name, printed in the list beside that argument on the command's help page and in the tool schema. No label may itself contain a semicolon followed by a space, because the guard over that list splits it on that pair.

reference.kind.workstream.context: One address kind a command's reference may name, printed in the list beside that argument on the command's help page and in the tool schema. No label may itself contain a semicolon followed by a space, because the guard over that list splits it on that pair.

refusal.at-capacity.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name at-capacity. {detail} carries the identifier, owner or column the refusal is about.

refusal.at-capacity.next.text: ; move a card out of {detail} first, or raise that column's wip_limit
refusal.at-capacity.next.context: Spliced onto refusal.at-capacity as the next step. {detail} is the column that has reached its limit.

refusal.at-capacity.next-operator.text: ; carry this through with --override yourself, move a card out of {detail} first, or raise that column's wip_limit
refusal.at-capacity.next-operator.context: Spliced onto refusal.at-capacity as the next step where the caller who was refused is the operator.

refusal.blocked.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name blocked. {detail} carries the identifier, owner or column the refusal is about.

refusal.blocked.next.text: ; ask the operator to lift it with `dinah unblock {card}`
refusal.blocked.next.context: Spliced onto refusal.blocked as the next step. {card} is the card reference the reader named.

refusal.dinah.add-needs-a-column.text: this workbench has no columns left to file a new card into
refusal.dinah.add-needs-a-column.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.add-needs-a-column. {detail} is the workbench.md path Add read an empty live columns list from, since l.refuse carries no path of its own for the malformed.at/.fix splice to reach.

refusal.dinah.add-needs-a-column.next.text: ; hand-edit {detail} to add a column to the columns list and create its columns/<id>/column.md, then run `dinah check` to confirm before trying `dinah add` again
refusal.dinah.add-needs-a-column.next.context: Spliced onto refusal.dinah.add-needs-a-column as the next step, carrying the clause that base entry used to end with. {detail} is the workbench.md path to hand-edit.

refusal.dinah.add-needs-a-column.next-na.text: ; hand-edit {detail} to add a column to the columns list and create its columns/<id>/column.md, then run `dinah check --workbench {workbench}` to confirm before trying `dinah add` again
refusal.dinah.add-needs-a-column.next-na.context: Spliced onto refusal.dinah.add-needs-a-column as the next step wherever a workbench was resolved for this invocation, which covers every reader standing in one and every reader who named one with --workbench from somewhere else. {workbench} is the workbench directory, and naming it is what lets the reader confirm the hand edit on the workbench he was filing into. {detail} is the workbench.md path to hand-edit. The sibling entry without the flag is the alternation's unconditional last member. The command spelling is machine vocabulary and is not translated.

refusal.dinah.already-withdrawn.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.already-withdrawn, which withdraw carries on an item that has already been withdrawn. {detail} is the state on disk, machine vocabulary that is never translated. refusal.dinah.already-withdrawn.next is spliced on after this one.

refusal.dinah.already-withdrawn.next.text: Reopen it first if it should be asked again.
refusal.dinah.already-withdrawn.next.context: The next step of refusal.dinah.already-withdrawn, spliced onto the sentence that just named the item's state.

refusal.dinah.ambiguous-card.text: more than one card answers to {detail}
refusal.dinah.ambiguous-card.context: The opening sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.ambiguous-card, naming the reference the reader typed. The candidate rows print beneath it, one 12-hex card identifier per row, and refusal.dinah.ambiguous-card.next follows as the closing line naming the way forward.

refusal.dinah.ambiguous-card.next.text: name one by the identifier above
refusal.dinah.ambiguous-card.next.context: The line printed after dinah.ambiguous-card's candidate rows, naming the way forward.

refusal.dinah.ambiguous-column.text: you can pull into more than one column right now
refusal.dinah.ambiguous-column.context: The opening sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.ambiguous-column, raised when the bare form of pull has more than one column in its qualifying set. The candidate rows print beneath it, one per qualifying column, and refusal.dinah.ambiguous-column.next follows as the closing line naming the way forward.

refusal.dinah.ambiguous-column.next.text: name one as `dinah pull <column>`, or pass --column <column>
refusal.dinah.ambiguous-column.next.context: The line printed after dinah.ambiguous-column's candidate rows, naming the ways forward.

refusal.dinah.ambiguous-name.text: {ordinals} on this card all answer to {selector}
refusal.dinah.ambiguous-name.context: The opening sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.ambiguous-name, carrying the ordinal of every attachment matching the selector. refusal.dinah.ambiguous-name.next follows as the closing line naming the way forward.

refusal.dinah.ambiguous-name.next.context: Spliced onto refusal.dinah.ambiguous-name as the next step, carrying the clause that base entry used to end with.

refusal.dinah.ambiguous-workbench.text: more than one workbench is reachable from {base}
refusal.dinah.ambiguous-workbench.context: The opening sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.ambiguous-workbench, naming the directory the search found several workbenches under. The candidate rows print beneath it, in the same shape the workbenches listing renders, and refusal.dinah.ambiguous-workbench.next follows as the closing line naming the ways forward.

refusal.dinah.ambiguous-workbench.next.text: choose one with --workbench <dir>, or run from inside it
refusal.dinah.ambiguous-workbench.next.context: The line printed after dinah.ambiguous-workbench's candidate rows, naming the ways forward.

refusal.dinah.at-loop-limit.text: this card has reached the loop limit of column {detail}
refusal.dinah.at-loop-limit.context: The sentence printed after the refusal name dinah.at-loop-limit. {detail} carries the column the card was leaving, which is where the loop_limit is declared and where the departures are counted.

refusal.dinah.at-loop-limit.next.text: ; ask the operator to carry this one move through with --override, or raise that column's loop_limit
refusal.dinah.at-loop-limit.next.context: Spliced onto refusal.dinah.at-loop-limit as the next step. An override carries the single move it is passed on and does not reset the count, so a later regressive move out of the same column is refused again.

refusal.dinah.at-loop-limit.next-operato.text: ; carry this one move through yourself with --override, or raise that column's loop_limit
refusal.dinah.at-loop-limit.next-operato.context: Spliced onto refusal.dinah.at-loop-limit as the next step where the caller who was refused is the operator.
